text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Morocco expects GDP to grow between 3.0 and 4.0 percent this year against 11.8 percent in 1996.
- Tourism sector needs reduction of red tape, better promotion and prices complying with quality standards.
- Palestinian Authority President Yasser Arafat says in message to King Hassan " Palestinian people need more support from Arab countries".

- Corruption hampers economic development and maintains poverty. No wonder that after scandal of school canteens and smuggling cases, World Food Programme, the World Bank and others are cautious about giving Moroco more help.
- Government determined to put an end to attempts to disturb normal course of studies at Casablanca university. Unrest over transport led to arrests and trials.
